paragraphs: There was once a man who travelled all over the land looking for a wife. He saw women young and old, rich and poor, pretty and plain, but could not find one he liked. At last he found a young, beautiful, rich woman whose right arm was solid gold. He married her immediately and thought no man was as lucky as he was. They lived happily together. But although he wanted people to think otherwise, he loved the golden arm more than all his wife’s other gifts put together.

At last she died. Her husband dressed in the blackest black and wore the longest face at her funeral. Despite that, he got up in the middle of the night, dug up her body and cut off the golden arm. He hurried home to hide his treasure, thinking no one would know.

The next night he put the golden arm under his pillow. He was just falling asleep when his dead wife’s ghost glided into the room. Stalking up to the bed, it pulled back the bed curtain and looked at him reproachfully. Pretending not to be afraid, he spoke to the ghost: ‘What have you done with your cheeks so red?’
‘All withered and wasted away,’ the ghost replied in a hollow voice.
‘What have you done with your red, rosy lips?’
‘What have you done with your golden hair?’
‘What have you done with your Golden Arm?’
